title: Customer key forensics and evidence automation for compliance
creator: Asha Patel
description: Scope: Build an automated pipeline that produces queryable, tamper-evident forensic artifacts for customer-managed keys (tenant KEKs and wrapping keys) across hosted/dedicated/private modes. Deliverables: (1) canonical evidence schema (signed snapshots + operation timeline), (2) HSM-aware collector agents that capture KMS/HSM rotation events, key material provenance markers, and policy-bound exports, (3) retention & redaction controls tied to customer retention settings, (4) automated delivery of proofs to a customer-facing evidence store (S3/GCS) and internal compliance buckets, (5) a lightweight query UI and API for temporal reconstruction of key state and rotation justification.
notes: Goals: enable auditors to reconstruct 'who/what/when' for a key lifecycle event within SLA; make artifacts machine-verifiable (signature chain); avoid shipping unnecessary key material; support multi-region proofs and cross-region residency stamping.
tradeoffs:
- Prefer HSM-signed event digests where tenant HSMs expose signing; fallback to agent-signed snapshots when HSM signing unavailable.
- Keep snapshot frequency configurable to balance cost vs. fidelity (default: event-driven + hourly checkpoint).
- Avoid storing plaintext key material; capture provenance metadata and sealed wrapping tokens only.
- Initial MVP focuses on rotation and import/export events; later phases cover transient KM operations (re-encrypt, unwrap).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Evidence JSON schema published and documented. 2) Collector agent deployed in dedicated & private test clusters capturing rotation events and producing signed snapshots. 3) Evidence delivered to evidence-bucket with access controls and lifecycle rules. 4) Demo: reconstruct a rotation timeline in the UI for a test tenant. 5) Automated test that verifies signature chain for 3 rotation scenarios.
